clue.text: Tintin's dance?

parts.note: split the boy reporter's name into tin plus tin, and each tin is a can, so the dance is two cans side by side

explanation.surface: A question about what dance the Belgian cartoon boy reporter might perform.
explanation.walkthrough: A tin is also a can, so 'Tintin' read as tin-tin becomes can-can, the high-kicking Parisian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking chorus-line dance from Parisian music halls.

clue.text: Roman foursome absorbed in sensual period of merrymaking

indicators.note: being absorbed in something means being taken inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: sensual means carnal, of the flesh
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four Romans lost in a period of sensual indulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: A carnival is a festival season of public revelry and feasting.

clue.text: Subject: Antonia's confusion in front of student

indicators.note: in this down clue the jumbled letters come in front of, so above, the next piece
a confusion of the woman's name means its letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: the name Antonia, its possessive adding no letter
L is the learner plate, a common abbreviation for a student

explanation.surface: Antonia is confused about a school subject, ahead of a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a school topic but is the noun for a citizen of a state.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a country, owing it allegiance, is called a subject or a national.

clue.text: In the morning one TV service is quite friendly

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon
I is the Roman numeral one
cable is a subscription television service

explanation.surface: A morning television service described as rather pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable describes relations that are cordial and good-natured, as between people on good terms.

clue.text: Greek and Latin races five in total

explanation.surface: Greek and Latin contestants, five of them racing in total.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse racing the Classics are five flat races for three-year-olds, including the Derby and the St Leger.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek and Latin studies are called the classics; British flat racing has five major races known by the same name.

clue.text: Its a shallow lake and girl turns up with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
O is the round figure zero, nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl appears naked beside a shallow lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water cut off from the sea by a reef or sandbank.

clue.text: One member in outer space is inadequate

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for outer space

parts.note: the sky stands for the heavens or space above
I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An astronaut in space is found lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre, scanty or not enough in amount.

clue.text: Fools do, and it is wrong

indicators.note: doing something wrong means getting it in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fools act, and it is the wrong thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of DO and IT IS; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Fools and idiots are both stupid people.

clue.text: Carol sits on the French one

indicators.note: in a down clue sitting on means placed above, so the first piece comes before

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone called Carol sits on a French object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name but is the verb meaning to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Single means solitary, just the lone individual.

clue.text: Keep tangled hairnet; get rid of husband

indicators.note: getting rid of something means removing it from what remains
a tangled net has its strands in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone should keep the tangled hairnet but get rid of the husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangled' rearranges HAIRNET; 'get rid of' then takes out H for husband, leaving RETAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to hold on to it, to hang on to possession.

clue.text: One gin and tonic cocktail (decarbonised) is what will get you started

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so these letters are mixed up
decarbonised means with the carbon taken away, and carbon's chemical symbol goes from the word tonic

explanation.surface: A gin and tonic cocktail promoted as the thing to get you going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decarbonised' removes C, the chemical symbol for carbon, from TONIC, leaving TONI; 'cocktail' mixes GIN with TONI to give GNITION after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: In a car the ignition is the system that fires the engine into life when the key is turned.

clue.text: Lives on oxygen except for making line on weather map

parts.note: lives means exists, is
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
bar means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: Someone lives on oxygen, apart from drawing lines on weather maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a contour joining points of equal atmospheric pressure on a meteorological chart.

clue.text: Ship a lot out from operating centre

indicators.note: out signals these letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Shipping many goods out from a business's operational base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operating centre' looks like a business base but is a place where surgeons operate.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical operations are carried out at a medical institution where patients are treated.

clue.text: Henry however catches one fish

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal
but means however
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man named Henry nevertheless lands a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish of northern seas, an example of the wider category.

clue.text: Organised one on river

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it, so the word for one comes after

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Somebody organised a single event on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or event is to manage or organise it.

clue.text: Are almost fit for producing crops

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: Something is nearly suitable for growing crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is ploughed and used for growing cereals and other harvests.

clue.text: Stop when duty requires it

indicators.note: the phrase requires the word inside it, so its letters lie within the clue words

explanation.surface: Someone stops working only when duty demands it.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words 'when duty'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop or finish something is to bring it to a close.

clue.text: Face attack

explanation.surface: Facing an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Mug is slang for the face, and to mug someone is to attack and rob them in the street.

clue.text: Venus is upset about To being jealous

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the moon's name
upset means knocked over, so the letters of the planet are disordered

parts.note: To is an OCR misreading of Io, a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: The planet Venus is upset about Jupiter's moon, out of jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' scrambles VENUS to ENVUS, and 'about' wraps that round IO. The paper's 'To' is an OCR slip for Io, a moon of Jupiter.
explanation.definitionFit: Envious and jealous both describe resentful desire for what another has.

clue.text: Authorise letters for road side notice

parts.note: to sign a document is to authorise it
post means letters and mail

explanation.surface: Approve the letters before putting a notice by the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost is a roadside board pointing travellers the way.

clue.text: He doesn't believe in jetlag -no stickler for tradition

indicators.note: in means the word is held within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A traveller who refuses to believe in jet lag, and doesn't care for tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known, so neither affirms faith nor denies it.

clue.text: Holds out for reduced price proposals

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
offers are proposed prices, as in a bid for a house

explanation.surface: A shop holds out for cut-price deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts PRO to PR. 'reduced price' reads as one phrase, but 'reduced' acts on 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: To proffer is to hold out or tender something for acceptance.

clue.text: It provides flavour and colour

explanation.surface: An ingredient that gives both taste and hue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a pungent spice root and also a reddish-orange shade of hair.

clue.text: Top chartered accountant goes on about climbing shrub

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going up, so the assembled pieces read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1, written AI, means top or first-class
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A leading accountant rambles on about a climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the whole run AICACA upside down. 'climbing shrub' looks like one phrase, but the acacia is a tree or bush, not a climber.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacias are thorny trees and bushes of warm regions, such as wattle.

clue.text: Is concerned about volume cuts

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: cares means is concerned

explanation.surface: Someone worries about volume cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to slice meat or wood with a blade.

clue.text: Risk is different French piste

indicators.note: being different means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a

explanation.surface: Taking risks is a different matter on a French ski slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A piste is a prepared downhill trail for skiers.

clue.text: Have a bath, however backward

indicators.note: backward means reading from right to left

parts.note: but means however

explanation.surface: Have a bath, though in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To tub is an old verb for washing in a bathtub.

clue.text: They have pull in high places

definitions.text: They have pull in high places

parts.words: They have pull in high places
parts.note: read pull literally: things that tow, which also rise high, rather than influential people

explanation.surface: Influential people with connections in the corridors of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pull' looks like influence, but it means towing: things that tow, as well as tall structures in high places.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall buildings stand high, and towing vehicles are things that pull.

clue.text: Two drugs — one idiot

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Two drugs make one fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or crazy person.

clue.text: Unique individual leading cricket side

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: one means a single individual
the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A unique player leading a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field facing the batter's bat, opposite the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something happening only once, without equal.

clue.text: Hide rent in bedspread

parts.note: to cover is to hide
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: Concealing torn fabric in a bedspread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' could be a tear, but here it is the verb meaning to lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A coverlet is a decorative top layer laid over a bed.

clue.text: Look at male with dislike

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: Glance at a man with distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, the strongest form of dislike.

clue.text: Telling one to go to blazes could encourage recidivism

definitions.text: Telling one to go to blazes could encourage recidivism

parts.words: Telling one to go to blazes could encourage recidivism
parts.note: telling someone to go to blazes is normally an insult, but read literally it urges a fire-raiser back to the fires

explanation.surface: A warning that cursing an offender may make them reoffend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go to blazes' is an insult, but read literally it sends someone off to fires; urging a fire-raiser to fires invites repeat offending.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sets fires deliberately as a crime commits arson.

clue.text: Keeps supplies of old punishment frames

explanation.surface: A store holding the old wooden frames used for punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop stocks goods it keeps on hand; the stocks were a wooden frame clamping offenders' ankles in public.
